title: VM provisioning and ./lab VM lifecycle
objective: Make the VM reproducible and controllable from the host: ./lab can provision or connect to the VM per #40, install Docker, transport the workspace, and run VM lifecycle commands idempotently. The host stops running the agent container itself.

acceptance_criteria.text: One documented command/runbook takes a clean host to a working VM (Docker plus compose plugin, repo checkout, agent image) with a CPU-only path that works without a GPU.
./lab gains VM lifecycle commands (names fixed by #40, for example vm up/status/ssh/down) that are idempotent: re-running does not duplicate VMs, disks or networks.

check_workspace() validation still runs on the host before a path is sent to the VM; /, $HOME, the lab repo without --unsafe-recurse, and sensitive credential directories are refused and never mounted.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Self-tests 1-6 pass: check_workspace rejects /, $HOME, sensitive dirs; accepts safe dirs; --unsafe-recurse allows repo

acceptance_criteria.text: The VM publishes no host ports by default; an automated check confirms the agent and workspace services are reachable only on the VM's internal Docker networks.

Model access follows #40: host-side ollama/llamacpp are reachable only through the narrow guestfwd ports; GPU passthrough is not required, and a CPU-only host starts with the same flow and a clear message.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: guestfwd entries configured for 11434, 8080, 3128 (code verified; live KVM test pending)

acceptance_criteria.text: ./lab stop removes agent containers plus workspace containers, networks and volumes and VM-side state; git status --short in the real checkout is empty afterwards.
./verify-lab.sh passes from a clean clone inside the VM, and the run is recorded on this ticket.

The host no longer runs the agent container; any host-side Docker use is limited to a documented service (for example model servers) if #40 chooses that option. README and docs/01-host-setup.md describe the VM flow and remove dev-container-only instructions.
Ability to test little-mester behavior within little-mester VM world using --unsafe-recurse (agent can read/write the repo inside the VM)
Full lifecycle test on real KVM host passes end-to-end: base → up → status → ssh → agent test → stop → down
Prereq check auto-detects distro, maps packages correctly, and prompts before installing
Idempotent lifecycle: re-running up/status/stop does not duplicate VMs or leave stale state
Troubleshooting: stale state is cleaned up correctly, orphaned processes are detected

A10: Full lifecycle test on real KVM host passes end-to-end: base → up → status → ssh → agent test → stop → down. Procedure: 1) Verify host KVM: grep -c svm /proc/cpuinfo > 0; 2) Verify /dev/kvm accessible; 3) ./lab-vm base (downloads image, verifies hash); 4) ./lab-vm up (creates overlay, seed ISO, starts virtiofsd + QEMU); 5) ./lab-vm status (confirms PID, port); 6) ./lab-vm ssh (opens shell, verify /workspace virtiofs mount, docker info); 7) cd /workspace && ./lab --unsafe-recurse; 8) git status --short clean; 9) ./lab-vm stop (graceful shutdown); 10) ./lab-vm down (teardown)

A11: Prereq check auto-detects distro, maps packages correctly, prompts before installing. Procedure: 1) ./lab-vm base with missing deps — detect distro, list missing tools; 2) Display distro-mapped package names; 3) Verify [y/N] prompt, default N; 4) On Arch: verify virtiofsd symlink fallback for /usr/lib/qemu/qemu-virtiofsd; 5) After install, re-run: 'All VM dependencies found. OK'

A12: Idempotent lifecycle — re-running up/status/stop does not duplicate VMs or stale state. Procedure: 1) Run ./lab-vm up twice, no second VM; 2) Run ./lab-vm stop twice, second is no-op; 3) ps aux | grep qemu-system-x86_64 ≤ 1; 4) ps aux | grep virtiofsd ≤ 1
A13: Stale state cleanup — manually killed QEMU, ./lab-vm status detects stale PID, ./lab-vm down cleans sockets/PIDs, no orphaned processes, fresh base+up works

needed: GPU-backed provisioning run or documented waiver
